title: マンション規約、変更しないと決議「無効」に？　要件緩和の落とし穴
extracted_text: 「マンション法」とも呼ばれる区分所有法が改正され、4月に施行されました。管理組合にとって影響が大きいのは、総会での決議要件の変更です。マンションのお金がかかわる議案の賛否に関係します。法改正に合わせた管理規約の見直しも必要ですが、もう済みましたか。 管理組合が開く総会では、議案ごとに賛否の決議をとる。役員選任などの「普通決議」は過半数、共用部分の大きな変更などの「特別決議」は4分の3以上、「建て替え決議」は5分の4以上など、議案によって可決の条件が違う。 今回改正されたのは、特別決議で多数決をとる際の計算方法だ。分母とする数字は3月まで、マンションを買った人（区分所有者）の全員だったが、4月からは総会出席者のみに変更された。 見直しの理由は、総会に参加しない無関心層がいることで決議に支障があったためだ。規約改正など適切な管理に必要な議案で、特別決議が必要なものは多い。ただ、区分所有者全員が分母だと、可決のハードルが高かった。総会出席者を分母にすれば、議案を通しやすくなる。 一方で、総会成立に必要な定足数も設けられ、特別決議をとるためには全区分所有者の過半数の出席が必要となる。直接参加だけでなく、委任状や議決権行使書を出した人たちも出席数に含む。 例えば、100戸のマンション（1戸1議決権と想定）では、総会に51戸が出席し、うち4分の3以上の39戸の賛成で可決。改正前は、4分の3にあたる75戸以上の賛成が必要だった。 国土交通省は今回の法改正に合わせ、より細かいルール「標準管理規約」を2025年10月に改正した。各管理組合はこの標準の規約をもとに、物件の実情に合った管理規約を設けており、それぞれにアップデートする必要がある。 自らのマンションの規約を変えないまま特別決議をとると、改正された区分所有法に抵触して無効となる恐れがある。決議のやり直しといった事態も起こりうる。 今回の改正は、マンション管理の停滞を防ぐ意味では重要です。ただし、決議しやすくなるほど、説明責任と合意形成の質が問われます。修繕・建て替え・規約変更は家計にも資産価値にも直結するため、管理会社任せではなく、住民側のガバナンス能力とコスト設計
translated_text: The Condominium Ownership Law, also known as the 'Mansion Law,' was amended and came into effect in April. The change that has the greatest impact on management associations is the revision of resolution requirements at general meetings. This affects the approval process for agendas involving condominium finances. While reviewing management rules to comply with the legal amendments is necessary, has your association already done so? At general meetings held by the management association, votes are taken on each agenda item. 'Ordinary resolutions' for items such as board member elections require a majority, 'special resolutions' for major changes to common areas require three-fourths approval, and 'rebuilding resolutions' require four-fifths approval—the threshold varies depending on the agenda. What changed this time is the calculation method for special resolutions. Until March, the denominator included all unit owners who had purchased units, but starting in April, it was changed to only those attending the meeting. The reason for the revision was that non-attending residents were hindering the resolution process. Many agendas necessary for proper management, such as rule amendments, require special resolutions. However, when all unit owners were in the denominator, the threshold for passage was too high. Using only meeting attendees as the denominator makes it easier to pass agendas. A quorum requirement has also been established: for special resolutions, more than half of all unit owners must attend. This includes those who participate directly as well as those who submit proxies or voting forms. For example, in a 100-unit building (assuming one vote per unit), if 51 units attend the meeting, passage requires 39 or more votes (three-fourths of attendees). Before the amendment, three-fourths of 100—meaning 75 votes—was required. In line with this legal amendment, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism revised the detailed 'Standard Condominium Management Rules' in October 2025. Each management association uses these standard rules as a basis to establish management rules tailored to their property's specific circumstances, meaning each needs to update them. If a special resolution is made without amending the association's rules, there is a risk it will be invalid under the amended Condominium Ownership Law. This could necessitate repeating the resolution process. This amendment is important in that it helps prevent stagnation in condominium management. However, while it makes resolutions easier, it raises questions about accountability and the quality of consensus-building. Since repairs, rebuilding, and rule changes directly impact household finances and property values, residents must not leave everything to the management company but instead strengthen their governance capabilities and cost planning.
title_en: Risk of 'Invalid' Resolution If Condominium Rules Not Amended? The Pitfall of Eased Requirements
